issue.title: Added color markup.
issue.body:
Continuing from discussion https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/issues/908

Markup syntax:
- **[name]** Sets the color by name. Names are currently hard-coded into a private static `ObjectMap<String,Color>` containing the same colors defined as constants in the Color class.
- **[#xxxxxxxx]** Sets the color specified by the hex value xxxxxxxx in the form  RRGGBBAA where AA is optional and defaults to 0xFF.
- **[]** Sets the color to the previous color (kind of optional end tag)
- **[[** Escapes the left bracket.

Color names are case-sensitive, cannot be empty, cannot start with `#` and cannot contain `]`. They can contain unescaped `[` though.

Markup is disabled by default. Use BitmapFont.setMarkupEnabled() to turn it on/off.

Support for user defined color names not implemented yet. Should they be stored in a static or member map?

body:
I would love to see this issue fixed!

On a side note: In a foolish attempt to contribute, I looked over the code of BitmapFontCache and, while not being able to do anything about the problem at hand, I noticed that one variable seems to be redundant: 
In line 69, `regionsLength` is declared, which is then used to declare the `vertexData` array in line 72 (`this.vertexData = new float[regionsLength][];`). Now without changing the array in between, the length of the array, which is still the same as `regionsLength`, is retrieved in line 75 and stored in a new variable `vertexDataLength`, which looks unnecessary to my inexperienced eye.
If however the benefit of ditching that one small int is insignificant and would just make the code harder to understand, consider this a pretty verbose "bump" :)

After looking at the code, I propose this:
BitmapFontCache gets a new datastructure, which saves a color and character count. The text colors are then described like this (example text: "Roses are [RED]red[], violets are [BLUE]blue[]"):
[Color.WHITE, 10], [Color.RED, 3], [Color.WHITE, 14], [Color.BLUE, 4]. It is set when the text is changed only.
setColor updates the vertex colors by multiplying the vertex data with the given color and the colors in the data structure above. this is of course only needed when the setColor color changes

issue.title: Nested Color Markup
issue.body:
Using "This is [RED]red with [YELLOW]yellow[] text[] inside" colors everything except for "yellow" in red. It seems like this is because only the previous color is stored. This could be solved by adding a color stack, which pops the top value when a "[]" is found.

body:
Ok before proceeding I need to know if I got it right.

> [Color.WHITE, 10], [Color.RED, 3], [Color.WHITE, 14], [Color.BLUE, 4]. It is set when the text is changed only.

Just to give things a name, let's call it `colorChunks`. It's updated by `BitmapFontChache.parseAndSetColor()` that adds a new chunk and it's cleared by `BitmapFontChache.clear()`

> setColor updates the vertex colors by multiplying the vertex data with the given color and the colors in the data structure above.

I guess you're talking about BitmapFontChache.setColors(Color) with the 's' at the end, which is called by Label.draw() and Window.draw() (so the color markup will work for window's title too, sounds good!).  However we are changing how setColors works, meaning that preexisting user code might have a different behavior since we no longer set vertex colors to the given color, but instead we mix it with the color from the corresponding chunk. 

> this is of course only needed when the setColor color changes

Sure I can compare the new and the old color which are float. However there are 3 overloaded setColors methods, and due to rounding errors they can generate slightly different float colors, so causing a check failure even when the two colors were actually the same. I guess this is not a real problem though.

Am I missing something?

First of all, imo the current implementation is bugged. If it breaks with the current behavior, so be it. I would expect setColor and setColors to change _only_ the glyphs that have default color since I explicitly entered specific colors for the rest. What's prolly needed is some kind of Color.Default. Each color chunk having this (not actually a) color, is tinted. Every other color stays as is. if everything shall be tinted, you can always disable the markup.

Tinting all glyphs, even those that have color set via mark up, seems quite
common. Eg fading in some text.
